title: A Secure Place for Bicycles
text:
The student transportation committee recommends converting 12 of the campus’s 286 car-parking spaces into a covered, lockable bicycle area for a one-year trial. The committee’s main claim is that secure bicycle storage would solve a specific barrier for students who already want to ride to campus without causing a serious parking shortage.

Campus security recorded 18 bicycle theft reports last academic year. Fourteen involved bicycles left at the uncovered racks beside the east classroom buildings. In a transportation survey, 37 percent of students who said they would consider cycling more often identified theft or weather exposure as a major concern. The committee argues that a monitored, covered storage area directly addresses both concerns.

Some drivers object that removing any car spaces will make morning parking worse. The committee responds that parking counts taken on twelve typical weekdays showed at least 34 unused spaces even during the busiest thirty-minute arrival period. It proposes placing the bicycle area at the edge of the east lot, where those counts found the most consistent unused capacity.

Another student group suggests that the college should instead expand discounted bus passes. The committee supports that idea as a separate transportation option but argues that bus discounts do not answer the storage problem faced by students who already own bicycles. The proposal therefore asks for a limited trial, followed by theft reports, bicycle-use counts, and parking counts before any permanent change.
author: Chee Skool
